newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares jump, seen extending gains.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares jump, seen extending gains.

text.p: Polish shares jumped in surging turnover and analysts saw them extending gains on Wednesday following Tuesday's strong buying after price fixing, but were not sure whether the tendency would continue.
The main market's WIG index rose 2.4 percent, to 14,772.1, and turnover jumped 56 percent to 153.2 million zlotys ($52.8 million) on both markets as 61 issues rose, five fell and 18 were flat.

"Perhaps it's a beginning of a longer tendency as we have rises in the whole Eastern European region, but the impetus of the growth suggests it might end soon," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
Some analysts said the WIG index might pierce the 15,000 psychological resistance as early as on Wednesday, but others said it was rather likely to end slightly below the barrier.
Some analysts said the Tuesday's growth might have been caused by foreign investors opening positions.

Analysts said Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), one of Warsaw bourse's large cap stocks surged 8.1 percent in the session's heaviest 20.2-million-zloty ($7 million) turnover possibly on a single large buy order.
They said it was difficult to explain the scale of construction firm Mostostal Warszawa's 9.9-percent surge, Mostostal Zabrze's 9.7 percent and glassmaker Krosno's 9.7-percent jumps.
Mass privatisation NFI units were flat in a 17.4-million ($6 million) turnover in the regular session and rose in 11.7-million-zloty ($4.0 million) continuous trade.
